newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura rises after job change announcement.
newsitem.headline: Nomura rises after job change announcement.

text.p: Shares of Nomura Securities Co Ltd firmed on Friday morning, following news that the brokerage would hold a news conference at 11.30 a.m. (0230 GMT) to announce a new president.
By 0145 GMT, Nomura's share price had climbed 20 yen to 1,400 yen. Volume was heavy at 4.734 million shares, the third largest on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Jiji news agency reported on Friday that Nomura chairman Masashi Suzuki will also take on the post of company president after the current president resigns.
Brokers said the likely shake-up of Nomura's top management has led some market players to believe that the effects of its recent scandal may be short-lived.

Nomura has been embroiled in controversy since it disclosed late last week that two of its directors made apparently illegal deals and funnelled funds to a corporate client that has been linked by Japanese media to a former "sokaiya" racketeer.
